content.intro: In this lesson, you will learn **Context Parameters** as part of **Advanced Kotlin Language Features**. String operations return values that should be handled explicitly; choose templates for interpolation and regular expressions only when pattern matching is the right abstraction. Use the subtopics—Context-Dependent Declarations, Reducing Repetitive Dependency Passing, Context Parameters and Explicit Context Arguments—as a checklist: predict what the example will do, then verify it in a project configured for the target platform.
content.why_it_matters: Professional applications need repeatable tests, clear APIs, dependable dependencies, security checks, and observable failures. Apply this concept in small steps before integrating it into a larger project.

items.title: Reducing Repetitive Dependency Passing
items.text: Reducing Repetitive Dependency Passing is part of reproducible project configuration. Declare the dependency or plugin where it belongs, preserve a compatible version set, and use the Gradle Wrapper for repeatable builds.

items.title: Context Parameters and Explicit Context Arguments
items.text: Context Parameters and Explicit Context Arguments describes how behavior is declared, passed, or composed. Make inputs and return types clear, keep side effects visible, and use a small call-site example to judge readability.

content_blocks.title: Common mistake to avoid
content_blocks.text: Explicit context arguments have the same stability level as context parameters.
